A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same autoformulation research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original NL4OPT and IndustryOR evaluations, search-efficiency measurements, critic analyses and supplementary recommendation experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds evaluations on MAMO and ComplexOR, search ablations, expert assessments and power-control solver simulations.

M1.justification: The four-stage MCTS, symbolic pruning, ranked priors, dual reward and deterministic parser remain. v2 adds a reported Best-of-N inference option selecting the complete path with the highest average node value (Appendix B.4), whereas v1 examines greedy recommendations after search (Appendix C.1.4). Top-three candidate retention was already present in v1.

E1.justification: v2 retains NL4OPT and IndustryOR and adds evaluation on MAMO's 211-problem ComplexLP subset and the 18 publicly available ComplexOR problems, expanding coverage of complex modeling problems. Appendix E also introduces empirical power-control solver simulations; this problem appeared only as a mathematical illustration in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds Tree-of-Thought implemented through depth-first search and naive sequential sampling as evaluated comparators on NL4OPT and IndustryOR (Table 6). The original main benchmark comparator set remains. However, v1's category-level comparison against ORLM (Table 3) is removed, although ORLM remains in aggregate comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported backbone changes from GPT4o-mini, with GPT4-1106 for NL4OPT, to GPT4-0613; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun. v2 adds candidate-count-matched ORLM sampling, Best-of-N evaluation, an expert review of 18 models, and original-versus-reformulated solver testing at 10 and 100 users. The existing 10-candidate, three-child and 16-rollout configuration remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds search ablations testing the contribution of guided exploration, expert analysis of component errors and correctness-proxy disagreements, and simulations examining reformulation and solver choice. It removes v1's detailed prior-ranking diagnostics, accumulated-prior analysis and lambda-dependent greedy-recommendation study. The main pruning, critic and rollout analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 removes Appendix C.1.2's prior-reward means, standard deviations, t-test and additional correlation analysis, while retaining the main-text reward correlations and p-values. Its new solver study reports aggregation over 100 random problem samples. Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty for the main benchmark accuracies.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result entries: Table 1 reports 62.3% on MAMO and 72.2% on ComplexOR after all rollouts; Tables 3–8 add expert-review, selected-output, matched-sampling, ablation and solver results. Several v1 appendix results disappear. The original Table 1 accuracies remain, including 92.62% on NL4OPT and 48.0% on IndustryOR; Table 2 changes are equivalent rounding. The reported backbone revision limits same-setting comparisons.

T1.justification: Equation (2) changes from optimizing model parameters for expected quality to selecting mathematical and computational formulations for quality. Appendix D substantially contracts the mathematical examples, removing weak-interference assumptions and their convexification derivation, power-flow models and the beamforming SOCP derivation. PC-MinPower is reclassified from Type I to Type II. The core taxonomy and SMT equivalence definitions are retained.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the novelty wording from formally introducing the concept of autoformulation to formalizing the problem as search. The central contributions—hierarchical LLM-guided MCTS, equivalence pruning, correctness evaluation and improved formulation performance—remain substantially the same.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation of practical reliability through expert-observed disagreements with objective-value correctness, constraint-modeling failures and deployment oversight requirements. It adds interpretations concerning entropy as an uncertainty indicator and reformulation-dependent solver performance. Conversely, v1's concrete ambiguity examples and discussion of weaknesses in greedy recommendations are removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproducibility section with implementation links, benchmark-access information and an explicit 5% execution-accuracy tolerance. These are new disclosures, not evidence that the tolerance changed. Most prompt templates are retained. Documentation remains imperfect: the relationship between the 244 NL4OPT problems in Section 5 and the 289 described in Appendix B.3 is not explained.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning against LLM planning and search methods, explicitly distinguishing hierarchical decomposition, symbolic pruning and comparative evaluation. It adds references concerning MAMO, self-consistency, self-rewarding models and active acquisition, while removing several references associated with deleted optimization examples. The main positioning relative to prior autoformulation frameworks remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations and discussion are extensively rewritten. Challenges receive a separate subsection, the problem taxonomy moves from Section 2.2 to Appendix C, method subsections are reordered, and appendices are reorganized. These are substantial narrative changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format. Figures 1–2 are redrawn, Figures 3–5 receive revised presentation, and Table 1 expands to four benchmarks. New tables present additional evidence, while Table 4 also redisplays existing Pass@N results. v1's Figures 6–9 and its category-level ORLM table are removed.

improvement.justification: v2's matched-candidate ORLM comparison, Best-of-N results, search ablations and expert audit make the evaluation more informative about practical use than v1's predominantly search-success comparisons. Implementation links also improve reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by removed statistical and sensitivity diagnostics and reporting inconsistencies: for example, four expert/proxy disagreements among 18 reviewed problems do not reconcile with the reported 82% agreement. The net improvement is useful but limited.
